Statement of Work — Adding Claude to STA's Salesforce

Integration options, trade-offs, and a recommended path
Prepared for: Adam Baker & STA Salesforce admin team Author: The Architect Date: 2026-06-01 Status: Draft for review

Objective

Connect Anthropic's Claude to STA's Salesforce org so the 4-person admin team can query, draft, and act on CRM data in natural language — without leaving the tools they already use. This SOW lays out every viable path, what each gives you, what each lacks, and a ranked recommendation.

Two directions — don't confuse them:

  • Outbound (Claude → Salesforce): Adam's Claude reads/acts on the org. This is the primary intent and where the options below focus.
  • Inbound (Claude inside Salesforce): Claude as the AI engine powering SF-side features (Prompt Builder, Agentforce agents) for end users. Covered as Option F.
Your data posture changes the math. STA's org holds no PII, no student data, and very limited customer data. That removes the "regulated workload" blocker that forces most orgs toward the heavy, fully-governed path. STA can safely use the lightweight, low-cost connectors that a district with student data could not. Translation: don't overpay for a trust boundary you don't need.

Recommendation

Winner — Salesforce Hosted MCP Server connected to Claude as a custom connector (Option A). Official, Salesforce-governed, team-wide, no code to maintain, and it works inside the Claude environment Adam already lives in. It is the durable answer.

Start this week — DX MCP Server, local (Option B) as a zero-cost, zero-license pilot for Adam. Prove the workflow in ~30 minutes, then graduate the team to Option A once the edition/Agentforce question (below) is settled.

⚠ One dependency gates Option A — confirm before committing. Hosted MCP requires Agentforce provisioned in the org (the sfap_api scope). It's free on Developer Edition, but a production Enterprise-Edition org may need Agentforce enabled and will meter usage in Flex Credits (~$0.10 per agent action). Action: Adam/Tanya verify STA's SF edition and whether Agentforce is provisioned. Until then, Option B carries the pilot at $0.

Ranked options & trade-offs

1

Option A — Salesforce Hosted MCP Server + Claude custom connector

Free on Dev Ed / credits in prod

Salesforce hosts the MCP server on its own infrastructure (Headless 360, 60+ tools across CRM, Data Cloud, Agentforce, Slack, workflows). You add it to Claude as a custom connector using an External Client App (OAuth 2.0 + PKCE). Adam then queries and acts on the org in plain language from Claude.

✅ Benefits

  • Official & supported by Salesforce — not a side project
  • Governed: respects SF permissions, sharing, and the user's own login scope
  • Bi-directional: read data and take governed actions
  • No code to maintain — Salesforce owns the server
  • Team-wide: each admin connects with their own permissions
  • Lives in Claude, where Adam already builds everything

What you'd lack / watch

  • Requires Agentforce provisioned (sfap_api scope) — the gating unknown
  • Prod usage meters Flex Credits (~$0.10/action)
  • Requires a paid Claude plan (Pro/Team/Max/Enterprise) for custom connectors
  • One-time admin setup of the External Client App + scopes
2

Option B — DX MCP Server, run locally

Free

A local MCP server launched via npx that uses your Salesforce CLI credentials. ~60 development/admin-focused tools (metadata, deploys, Apex tests, queries). No OAuth app, no Agentforce license. Setup ~30 minutes.

✅ Benefits

  • $0 and fast — running today, no procurement
  • No Agentforce / edition dependency
  • Tuned for admin/dev work — perfect for Adam (owns Flows & metadata)
  • Uses the same CLI OAuth flow you already trust; creds stay local

What you'd lack

  • Local-only — tied to one machine, not a team service
  • Dev-oriented; thinner for business-user querying
  • Depends on the CLI being installed/authorized
  • No central governance or audit beyond the SF user's scope
3

Option C — Community / open-source MCP server

Free

Third-party MCP implementations (e.g. github.com/tsmztech/mcp-server-salesforce) offering simple read/write with username-password or OAuth login.

✅ Benefits

  • Free and flexible; broad CRUD access
  • Works on any edition; no Agentforce needed
  • Good for a quick proof-of-concept if A and B don't fit

What you'd lack

  • No Salesforce support and you own the maintenance
  • Third-party code touching the org — security review needed even with low-PII
  • Username/password auth patterns are weaker than PKCE OAuth
  • Superseded by the official A/B paths for most needs
4

Option D — Agentforce 360 + Claude native partnership

Credits / seats

The deep Anthropic–Salesforce partnership: Claude models run inside the Salesforce trust boundary, with bi-directional MCP Apps that bring SF context into Claude and trigger governed Agentforce actions. Rolling out across 2026, starting with Slack.

✅ Benefits

  • Most governed; data stays in SF-managed VPCs
  • Trigger native Agentforce actions from Claude
  • Slack-first — and STA uses Slack
  • Strategic / future-proof direction

What you'd lack / why not now

  • The trust-boundary selling point is low value for STA (no PII)
  • Needs Agentforce; conversation (~$2) or credit costs
  • Premium seats (Agentforce add-ons $125–$150/user/mo; Agentforce 1 from $550/user/mo) are unjustifiable here
  • Still rolling out through 2026 — not all GA
5

Option E — Dedicated Salesforce user + Claude in Chrome

~1 SF seat

Provision a licensed "Claude" Salesforce login and let Claude drive the SF UI through the browser. The brute-force path when an API/MCP route isn't available.

✅ Benefits

  • Works on any SF edition — no MCP or Agentforce needed
  • Can reach anything a human can click, including no-API screens
  • Useful for one-off UI tasks or verification

What you'd lack

  • Brittle — UI changes break the automation; slow vs API
  • Costs a full SF seat and creates an autonomous-login security surface
  • No governance/audit advantages
  • Against The Architect's own posture (browser is read-only by default)
6

Option F — Einstein / Models API (Claude inside Salesforce)

Credits

Use Claude as the LLM behind Salesforce-native AI — Prompt Builder templates, Flow-invoked generation, Agentforce agents serving SF end users. This is the inbound direction, a different job than A–C.

✅ Benefits

  • AI surfaces directly in Salesforce for end users (e.g. Help Center / Experience Cloud)
  • Governed by SF Prompt Builder grounding and guardrails
  • Reuses Adam's Flow expertise

What you'd lack

  • Doesn't give Adam Claude-side control of the org (different use case)
  • Needs Einstein/Agentforce setup and credits
  • Only worth it if there's a defined end-user AI feature to ship
7

Option G — Custom Anthropic API + Apex/Flow callout

Build cost

Hand-build the integration: Anthropic API key, Named Credential, Apex callouts or Flow HTTP callouts wiring Claude into custom org logic.

✅ Benefits

  • Total control over behavior and data flow
  • Can embed Claude in any bespoke automation

What you'd lack

  • Build + maintenance burden the official MCP paths remove
  • API key/secret management overhead
  • Reinvents what Options A/B/F give for free or near-free

Recommended next steps

  1. Confirm the gating fact (Adam/Tanya): STA's Salesforce edition and whether Agentforce is provisioned (sfap_api scope). This decides Option A's cost.
  2. Run the Option B pilot this week (Adam): install Salesforce CLI, authorize the org, create .mcp.json, connect from Claude. ~30 min, $0. Validate real admin workflows (e.g. query renewals, draft Flow logic).
  3. Stand up Option A for the team once the edition question is settled: create the External Client App (callback URL, "Access MCP servers" + "Perform requests at any time" scopes, PKCE on), add as a Claude custom connector, each admin connects with their own login.
  4. Park Options D & F as a future "watch" item — revisit only if STA defines a customer-facing AI feature for the Experience Cloud Help Center.
  5. Skip C, E, G unless A and B both prove unworkable.
